article.title: Everyday phone call phrases
article.description: Answering: 'Hello, this is [name] speaking.' Asking to hold: 'Could you hold on a second?' Ending: 'Thanks for calling, talk soon!' Common mistake: 'I am [name]' on the phone sounds unnatural in English — 'This is [name]' is the standard phone convention.
article.content: Answering: 'Hello, this is [name] speaking.' Asking to hold: 'Could you hold on a second?' Ending: 'Thanks for calling, talk soon!' Common mistake: 'I am [name]' on the phone sounds unnatural in English — 'This is [name]' is the standard phone convention.

generated.caption:
Ever said "I am [name]" when answering the phone? It sounds unnatural to native English speakers! Instead, the standard way is "Hello, this is [name] speaking." Need someone to hold? "Could you hold on a second?" is perfect. To end a call politely, try "Thanks for calling, talk soon!"

Save this for smooth English calls, share with a friend, and follow @TheEnglishVault for daily tips!
generated.script:
Phone pe bolte ho “I am [name]”? Ye mistake almost sab karte hain!

Dekho, jab English mein phone call pe khud ko identify karna ho, “I am [name]” bolna sounds unnatural. Standard aur correct tareeka hai: “Hello, this is [name] speaking.” Jaise, “Hello, this is Maya speaking.” Aur agar kisi ko hold pe rakhna hai, toh bolo “Could you hold on a second?” Call end karte time, bolo “Thanks for calling, talk soon!”

Ab samajh aaya? Next time phone pe, confidently bolo “Hello, this is [name] speaking!” Not “I am [name]”!

slides.headlineRest: — Is Actually Wrong on the Phone
slides.body: On the phone, saying 'I am [name]' can sound unnatural to English speakers. The standard and polite way to introduce yourself is 'Hello, this is [name] speaking.' For example, when you answer a call, you'd properly say, 'Hello, this is Sarah speaking.' Beyond introductions, other useful phrases include asking someone to hold: 'Could you hold on a second?' And when ending a call: 'Thanks for calling, talk soon!'
